keep: Don't take my word for it. Look at the stones.
1208 BCE, an Egyptian pharaoh carved a victory stone.
9th century BCE, a stone in Dan mentions the house of David.
Around 700 BCE, under Jerusalem, workers carved a tunnel inscription in Hebrew.
Around 600 BCE, like a hundred years later, two tiny silver scrolls with a priestly blessing.
The oldest Bible text ever found.
132 CE, coins from the revolt say, for the freedom of Jerusalem.
Other peoples lived here too, and their stones are here as well.
But stones don't lie. Jews were here.
Comment HISTORY, and I'll send you the sources.
